turns.replyText:
Can you explain the main options in simple terms?

Sure, here's the simplest way to think about it. There are three main categories:

Blinds have individual slats that tilt open or closed, so you can fine-tune light and privacy without raising the whole thing up. Popular styles include Faux Wood, Wood, Mini, Aluminum, and Vertical Blinds. 

Shades are made from one continuous piece of fabric that lifts and lowers as a single unit. Some roll up neatly, others fold into soft pleats. Types include Roller, Roman, Cellular (Honeycomb), Zebra, Solar, Sheer, Woven Wood, and Pleated Shades.

The quick trick to remember the difference: slats = blinds, fabric = shades.

Shutters are solid hinged panels, often called plantation shutters. They're durable, timeless, and great for light control, but they come with some trade-offs compared to blinds and shades.

Is there anything else a beginner needs to get started?

Here's a quick checklist to make sure you're all set:

1. Free swatches - Before ordering, grab some free samples so you can see and feel the actual color and material in your own lighting. Screens can be misleading, and seeing it in person makes a big difference. You can order up to 15 free samples at a time to compare side by side. 

2. Measure your windows - This is the most important step. Use a steel tape measure, and write down width first, then height. The measuring guide walks you through inside vs. outside mount for each product type. Every product has slightly different requirements, so check the Specifications tab on the product page too.

3. Pick your mount type - Inside mount fits within the window frame for a clean, built-in look. Outside mount goes over the frame and gives better light coverage. Either works, it just depends on your window and preference.

A few things you don't need to worry about: shipping is free, every order comes with a free 3-year limited warranty, and there's a measuring protection guarantee in case something's off.

How do I use it properly the very first time?
10:07 PM

Here's a simple walkthrough for first-timers:

Installing:



Clean the surface where the adhesive will stick (aluminum, wood, PVC, vinyl, or painted surfaces all work)


Peel the backing off the adhesive brackets


Press them firmly onto your window frame


Snap the shade into place on the brackets



No tools needed, that's the whole thing. For detailed step-by-step diagrams, you can grab the installation guide PDF too. 

Operating:
Just push up on the bottom rail to raise the shade, and pull down to lower it. That's it, no cords or wands to fuss with.

If you ever need to remove them:
Warm the adhesive with a hair dryer for 20-30 seconds, then slowly peel from a corner. Any leftover residue rubs off with a soft cloth.

One thing to keep in mind: make sure you have at least 1 1/8" of depth for an inside mount, or 1 1/8" of flat surface for an outside mount.
